title: West Asia war, the Strait of Hormuz and India’s oil bill
dek: How the US–Iran conflict disrupted the world’s most important oil route, and why it matters so much to India.
seoTitle: Strait of Hormuz crisis 2026: oil and India
status: US disables blockade runner; Brent near $97.50
bigLabel: Brent during Friday morning trading on 27 Nov (11:30 am UAE time), per The National; on track for a weekly gain of about 7%. Brent settled at $94.61 on 25 Nov and $89.37 on 23 Nov, a three-month low.

glance.what: Since the war began, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted. Brent peaked near $118 in late October, then fell sharply in November as Qatar mediated talks between Iran and the US, before rebounding on fresh attacks.
glance.why: India imports most of its crude oil, and a large share of its oil, LNG and almost all its LPG has passed through Hormuz. The government says it absorbed ₹43 of a needed ₹50-a-litre diesel increase.
glance.next: Brent was near $97.50 on 27 November, on track for a weekly gain of about 7%. US forces disabled a ship that tried to breach the blockade of Iran, Central Command said, and Iran offered to help Kuwait and Italy investigate the drone attack that killed two Italian technicians, which it denies carrying out. Brent rose for a third day, to about $96, on 26 November. Saudi Arabia says a projectile hit its Jazan refinery, killing a worker and halting some operations; the Saudi-led coalition blames the Houthis, who also claim a strike on Ras Tanura. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two tankers hit mines near Hormuz, which has not been confirmed. Qatar is trying to revive US–Iran talks. OPEC+ meets on 29 November. A drone attack on an air-defence site in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians on 26 November; Kuwait blames Iran, which denies it.

forYou: Higher oil prices feed into petrol, diesel, cooking gas and airfares, and weaken the rupee.

upcoming.label: 29 Nov
upcoming.text: OPEC+ ministers meet to set output for 2027

next: Whether Qatar can restart US–Iran talks; more attacks on Saudi oil sites and tankers in Hormuz; OPEC+ meets on 29 November to set 2027 output.

events.title: Strikes on Iran; the Strait of Hormuz closes
events.summary: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran, Hormuz shipping is shut. Brent ends the week near a seven-month high of about $73.

events.title: Tankers hit; shipping lines suspend Hormuz routes
events.summary: At least three tankers are damaged and Maersk suspends all cargo through the strait. Brent closed above $79 on 3 March, up from about $65 before the crisis.

events.title: Brent crosses $100
events.summary: Oil climbs back above $100 a barrel as the disruption drags on.

events.title: Blockade continues as peace talks stall
events.summary: Brent trades at $102.40 on 23 April and above $106 the next day.

events.title: Ceasefire news brings relief
events.summary: Brent falls about 4% to around $84 on news of a ceasefire and hopes that Hormuz shipping will normalise.

events.title: Oil back above $90
events.summary: A US–Iran deadlock keeps Hormuz disrupted, raising India’s import bill and pressure on the rupee.

events.title: Brent nears $100 again
events.summary: A fresh escalation in the US–Iran conflict renews fears for Gulf supplies, with Hormuz shipping still severely disrupted.

events.title: Saudi pipeline hit; Brent above $107
events.summary: An Iranian ship is attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline, used to bypass the strait, is damaged in a drone attack. Brent crosses $107 even as the US says it is escorting more tankers.

events.title: Oil peaks near $118
events.summary: Brent climbs to a late-October peak of about $118 a barrel after tankers are struck in the strait, its highest close in six months.

events.title: Qatar talks: oil plunges about 8%
events.summary: After weekend mediation talks between Iran and Qatar, a draft proposal to end the war circulates, reportedly centred on reopening Hormuz. Brent settles 7.6% lower, even as tankers near the strait are hit.

events.title: Iran's Hormuz plan goes to the White House
events.summary: Qatar's prime minister takes an Iranian proposal to reopen Hormuz to President Trump. Under the reported plan, the US would lift its blockade and release $8 billion in frozen funds. A Qatari official called one report of the terms false. Brent falls to its lowest close since 31 August.
events.differs: An Israeli outlet reported Iran had dropped its demand to charge tolls in the strait; a Qatari official told Bloomberg that report was false.

events.title: Brent briefly drops below $90
events.summary: Brent dips under $90 for the first time since August as Hormuz flows recover to near pre-war levels, then rebounds after Iran denies it is negotiating with Washington and more ships are attacked.

events.title: Trump says no deal needed; oil jumps 3%
events.summary: Trump posts that the US does not need a deal with Iran. Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy sites, and Iran's military reports tankers hit in the strait. Brent settles 3.3% higher at $95.82. In India, PM Modi says the government absorbed ₹43 of a needed ₹50-a-litre diesel increase.

events.title: Oil ends a second losing week; IEA sees a surplus
events.summary: Brent settles 2 cents higher at $95.84 a barrel after swinging in a $2 range, its second weekly fall in a row. The International Energy Agency (IEA), which advises rich countries on energy, says the oil market will be in surplus this quarter for the first time since the war began, as high prices have cut demand. Iran said four tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz the day before.

events.title: Iran fires drones at a US base in Bahrain, twice in three days
events.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) say they sent six drones at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain on Sunday, aiming at US military equipment, in retaliation for US strikes on Iran, including on Qeshm Island. It was the second such attack in three days: on Friday the IRGC said it hit a US early-warning radar there. Bahrain says its air defences intercepted the drones. The US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) said it shot down two drones on Friday with no injuries or damage, and a spokesman said there were "no impacts to American forces" on Sunday. The Washington Post says Bahrain had been relatively quiet for months. Iran's foreign ministry said Tehran would keep responding to "military aggression". On Monday morning in India, Brent crude was trading about 1% lower at $94.85 a barrel, PTI reported.
events.status: Stated · IRGC, Bahrain, CENTCOM; Market data · PTI
events.differs: Iran's described target differs: "U.S. military equipment at a helicopter base" (Washington Post) versus "a U.S. air defense radar system" (SOFX).

events.title: Brent falls below $92 as Gulf exports recover
events.summary: Brent crude fell 78 cents to $91.66 a barrel by 0430 GMT on Tuesday (10 am in India), Reuters reports, after a sharp fall on Monday. JournalArta puts Monday's drop at 3.5%, to $92.44. Traders say recovering oil exports from the Middle East and expectations of a supply surplus outweigh continued Iranian attacks on US bases in Bahrain and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. ANZ analysts say traffic through Hormuz is still only 49% of pre-war levels. Goldman Sachs expects a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day in 2027. OPEC+ meets on 29 November to decide output for 2027.

events.title: Tankers hit near Hormuz; Iran strikes at a Kuwait base; Riyadh tower damaged
events.summary: An ADNOC product tanker was hit by an 'unknown projectile' north of Khasab, Oman, at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one seafarer missing and 11 injured, ADNOC's shipping arm confirmed, per Seatrade Maritime. A second tanker was hit in its engine room near Khasab on 18 November; its crew are safe, per Gulf News and Arab News. Nobody has claimed either attack. On 17 November a US fighter struck what a US official called an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in 'self-defense', after Iranian drones targeted US forces in Bahrain, per TIME. On 18 November Iran attacked Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, which hosts US forces, and targets in Bahrain; both countries said they repelled the attacks, per The Hill and TIME. Iranian military units separately claimed that tankers hit mines east of Hormuz; this has not been independently confirmed. On 19 November a Houthi attack damaged the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh, with no injuries reported, per Al Jazeera and The National. Despite this, Brent settled at $91.95 on 18 November, down 1.28%, as US stockpiles rose, Reuters reports.
events.status: Reported · Seatrade, Gulf News, TIME, Al Jazeera
events.differs: Seatrade dates the ADNOC tanker strike to the evening of 17 November; Arab News puts it on 18 November. Iran's army says three tankers hit mines; the Revolutionary Guards' navy says two. In Riyadh, the Saudi-led coalition says the damage came from debris of intercepted missiles; the Houthis claim a direct hit.

events.title: Oil heads for a third weekly fall as Gulf exports recover
events.summary: Oil prices were on course for a third weekly fall in a row on Friday, Reuters reported via RTÉ, as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels, raising expectations of a supply surplus. Brent fell below $91 a barrel by 11 am New York time, per Al-Monitor, and PTI reported it 1.82% lower at $90.31 during Indian trading hours. Earlier in the day, Brent had risen to $92.57 after a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh and an Iranian Revolutionary Guards claim that two tankers hit mines in Hormuz and were burning; that claim has not been independently confirmed. Saxo analysts also pointed to a sell-off in AI-linked shares weighing on demand expectations. UOB analysts say Iranian attacks on tankers are running at about one a day in November. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.
events.status: Market data · Reuters, PTI; Stated · IRGC (mines claim)
events.differs: Reuters via RTÉ, writing on Friday morning, put Brent's weekly fall at 3.5%; Al-Monitor, later in the day, said about 5%.

events.title: Brent settles at $92.57, ending a third weekly fall
events.summary: Brent crude for January rose 0.6% on Friday to settle at $92.57 a barrel, but fell 3.4% over the week, its third weekly fall in a row, per Bloomberg via Rigzone. FinanceFeeds gives the same settlement and says Brent was $95.84 a week earlier. Brent is down about a fifth in November, per Bloomberg. Traders weighed the risk of new US strikes on Iran against plentiful supply as Gulf exports recover; the IEA expects a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter. US WTI crude for January rose 1.2% to $83.41. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.
events.differs: FinanceFeeds links Friday's rise to reports of a tanker fire near Hormuz; Bloomberg does not mention one on Friday and points to the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran.

events.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they shot down a US drone over Hormuz
events.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Saturday that its forces shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz with a newly deployed air defence system, per Iranian state media cited by ANI and Middle East Eye. The IRGC called it the 58th MQ-9 brought down by Iranian forces. No US confirmation or denial had been reported. Al Jazeera, via Occasional Digest, reports that efforts to end the war remain stalled: Iran's foreign minister said its conditions must be met for the strait to reopen, and President Trump said Tehran wants a deal but not one he can accept.
events.status: Allegation · IRGC (not confirmed by the US)

numbers.k: MQ-9s Iran says it has downed

events.title: Two tankers hit leaving Hormuz; Iran fires missiles and drones at US bases in Bahrain
events.summary: Early on Saturday two tankers leaving the Gulf were hit by unknown projectiles, one about 20 km north of Khasab in Oman and one about 31 km east of it, said UKMTO, the British agency that tracks shipping. One was hit in the stern and one in the engine room; no one was reported hurt. Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted zone east of the strait; it is not clear if this was one of the two. On Saturday night Iran launched drones and ballistic missiles at US bases in Bahrain, per Iranian media cited by Euronews. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted several attacks and a fire broke out at a civilian industrial site, with no injuries. The Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said they hit two Patriot missile batteries and a radar; Bahrain and the US have not confirmed this. The US military denied a separate IRGC claim that Iran damaged a US F-16 jet on Friday. Iran's deputy foreign minister said more than 14 Iranian tankers are ready to sail through the US blockade to China, and warned of a 'fierce military response' if they are stopped.
events.status: Confirmed · UKMTO (tankers), Bahrain (fire); Allegation · IRGC (Patriot strikes, F-16, denied by US)
events.differs: Al Jazeera says about 25 shipping incidents have been reported in the past week, citing Iran's armed forces; this has not been independently confirmed.

numbers.k: Iranian tankers waiting to sail (Iran's claim)

events.title: Bahrain says two people were hurt in Saturday's Iranian attack on an industrial plant
events.summary: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said two people were injured when Saturday's Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial plant and started a fire: a Bahraini citizen, who is stable, and a Pakistani resident, who is in a critical condition. Earlier official statements had said no one was hurt. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said the site was 'a purely civilian industrial facility', rejected Iran's reasons for the attack and said it keeps the right to defend itself under the UN Charter. The Revolutionary Guards said they had targeted US Patriot air-defence radars at two bases in Bahrain; this has not been confirmed.
events.status: Confirmed · Bahrain Interior Ministry; Allegation · IRGC (Patriot radars)
events.differs: Iranian media cited by Gulf News named different US bases (Sheikh Isa and Juffair) from those in the IRGC statement reported by The National (Al Riffa and Awali).

events.title: Iran says two supertankers hit mines east of Hormuz; UKMTO reports a tanker 'incident with military forces'
events.summary: Iran's navy said on Sunday that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the ships had switched off their tracking systems and entered a 'forbidden' area, per Xinhua. The Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) navy separately said two supertankers exploded on 'unauthorized' routes north of Oman's Al Ghanam Island. The ships were not named and no one else has confirmed the incident. On Sunday evening UKMTO, the British agency that tracks shipping, said a tanker 'was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman', near Chabahar, and that investigations were under way, per Euronews. It gave no ship name or casualties. Euronews says the area is near the US blockade line, but it is not known whether this involved one of the Iranian tankers said to be ready to test the blockade. The IRGC also said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone east of the strait; the US has not commented.
events.status: Stated · Iran's navy and IRGC (mine hits, drone; not independently confirmed); Reported · UKMTO (Gulf of Oman incident)
events.differs: Middle East Eye says it is unclear whether the UKMTO incident is linked to the two tankers Iran described.

events.title: Trump says he could resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail
events.summary: In a Fox News interview, President Trump said he was inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail, per Arab Times and Iran International. Asked about Iranian tankers testing the US blockade, he said: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," per Arab Times. Iran International quotes him as saying: "I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent." Indirect talks continue, with Qatar passing messages, Arab Times reports. Iran's parliament speaker said a state of 'neither war nor peace' cannot continue, and a deputy foreign minister said Iran is still talking to the US but is ready for any scenario, per Iran International. No decision to strike has been announced.
events.differs: Arab Times dates the interview to Sunday 22 November; Iran International dates it to Saturday 21 November and only paraphrases the remarks on strikes and sinking ships.

events.title: Brent falls to a three-month low as Gulf exports hold up
events.summary: Brent crude for January delivery settled at $89.37 a barrel on Monday, down about 3.5% from $92.57 on Friday and its lowest in about three months, per FinanceFeeds and Kotak Neo. Analysts said signs that Gulf crude exports are holding up outweighed weekend attacks on shipping and on Bahrain, per Investing.com and Tradingpedia. Libya's Sharara pipeline also reopened. The International Energy Agency expects supply to exceed demand by about 2 million barrels a day in October–December. Analysts at IG said a new US strike on Iran looks less likely for now. Lower oil prices help India, which imports most of its crude.
events.differs: This page first gave Monday's settlement as about $86.6–86.8, per Investing.com and houseofsaud.com. FinanceFeeds and Kotak Neo give $89.37 for the January contract, which fits Bloomberg's report of a 2.3% rise to $91.40 on 24 November. The lower figures are close to the February contract (about $86.5 on 24 Nov, per FinanceFeeds) and may refer to it.

events.title: Iran vows to confront the US blockade; says Hormuz could be safe again if its terms are met
events.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran would "definitely not tolerate" the US naval blockade and would "use all our tools" to confront it, per ABC News. He said security in the Strait of Hormuz could be restored quickly if the US lifts sanctions, ends the blockade and carries out the terms of the June memorandum of understanding. Oil shipped through Hormuz averaged about 9.5 million barrels a day in the 10 days to 19 November, down from 12.2 million in October, per Kpler data cited by Reuters. Iran began rationing electricity on 22 November because of fuel shortages, ABC reports.

numbers.v: ≈ 9.5 mbpd (10 days to 19 Nov) vs 12.2 mbpd in Oct (Kpler)

events.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three more tankers hit mines in Hormuz despite a US escort
events.summary: The navy of Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said on Monday that three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz over the previous few hours, per Iranian state media cited by Iran International. It said one was hit near the southern coast and two east of the strait, and that a US military escort failed to prevent this. "The Strait of Hormuz is not a place to test unauthorized routes or ignore maritime warnings," the IRGC said. The ships were not named and no casualties were reported. The claim has not been independently confirmed, and US Central Command had not responded at the time of reporting, per The Sunday Guardian. This is a separate claim from Iran's report on Sunday of two tankers hitting mines.
events.differs: Iran International describes the US escort as an air escort; The Sunday Guardian says only that the US military was escorting the ships.

events.title: US sanctions 22 companies and 8 people it links to Iran's oil money networks
events.summary: The US Treasury announced new sanctions on Monday against 22 entities and eight individuals it says help move money for Iran's oil trade and tanker fleet, per gCaptain and Iran International. Most of the companies named are in Dubai, with others in Hong Kong and Turkey, Iran International reports. Sanctions bar them from dealing with US banks and businesses. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said "Iran's shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime," per Iran International. A separate Treasury analysis found $14.7 billion in transactions that may be linked to these networks, it reports.

events.title: Three tankers hit near Hormuz; Iran's army chief says the strait must be 'closed further'
events.summary: Three Liberian-flagged supertankers owned by South Korea's Sinokor were hit within about 20 minutes on the evening of 22 November (UTC) as they left the eastern end of the Strait of Hormuz, per a revised UKMTO report cited by Maritime Executive. All crew were accounted for and the ships carried on. It is not clear whether these are the ships Iran says hit mines. On 23 November Iran's army commander, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, said Hormuz "must be closed further day by day" until Iran's seven conditions are met, per Euronews. Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said there would be "no negotiation" before then. The same day Qatar's prime minister met US Vice-President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington to try to restart US–Iran talks, per AP.
events.status: Reported · UKMTO (tankers); Stated · Iranian officials; Confirmed · US State Department (Qatar meetings)
events.differs: Marine Insight says it is unclear whether the ships in UKMTO's reports are the same ones Iran says hit mines; Iran has not named its ships.

events.title: Brent rebounds 2.3% to $91.40 on new tanker attacks
events.summary: Brent crude for January rose 2.3% to settle at $91.40 a barrel on Tuesday, after early losses, per Bloomberg (via Rigzone) and Seeking Alpha. US crude (WTI) rose 2.4% to $82.05. Reports of more attacks on ships near Hormuz, and Iran's vow to tighten control of the strait, outweighed signs of a supply surplus. The IEA says Gulf crude exports are back to 74% of pre-war levels, per Bloomberg. Trading was thin before the US Thanksgiving holiday, which can exaggerate moves.

events.title: Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery; Saudi-led coalition says it downed four drones
events.summary: Yemen's Houthis said on 25 November they made a "direct" strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, causing fires, and attacked Riyadh's financial district, per The National and Anadolu Agency. The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura. It did not say the refinery was hit, and the claim could not be independently verified. Ras Tanura is also a major Saudi crude export terminal. A day earlier, on 24 November, a drone strike on a tower in Riyadh's financial district wounded 11 people, Saudi civil defence said. The tower houses the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's state wealth fund, and was hit for the second time in a week.
events.status: Allegation · Houthis (refinery strike); Stated · Saudi-led coalition (drones downed); Confirmed · Saudi civil defence (Riyadh injuries)

events.title: Brent jumps 3.5% to $94.61 after the Houthi refinery claim
events.summary: Brent crude for January rose $3.21, or 3.5%, to settle at $94.61 a barrel on Wednesday, its second daily gain in a row, per Reuters (via The Circuitry) and the Wall Street Journal (via The Library). US crude (WTI) rose 2% to $83.68. Traders cited the Houthi claim of an attack on Ras Tanura, traders closing bets on lower prices before the US Thanksgiving holiday, and a smaller-than-expected rise in US crude stocks. Expectations of a supply surplus limited the gains. OPEC+ meets on 29 November to set output for 2027.
events.differs: Finexus gives a Brent settlement of $94.26 (+4.7%) and WTI of $83.78; Reuters and the WSJ give $94.61 and $83.68.

numbers.k: US crude stocks, week to 20 Nov

events.title: Strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery kills a worker and halts some operations; Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines
events.summary: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said a "hostile aerial projectile" hit the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast on 26 November, starting a fire and forcing some operations to stop, per Arab News. One Nepali worker was killed and several were injured. The refinery can process up to 400,000 barrels a day. The Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis and said it destroyed a missile launch platform at Hodeidah port used in the attack. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines north of Khasab, Oman, while crossing the Strait of Hormuz by an "unauthorised route", per the semi-official Tasnim agency. They said one was a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels. The ships were not named and the claim has not been independently confirmed. The UK's maritime agency UKMTO reported an explosion near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai the same day; it is not clear if this was the same incident.
events.status: Confirmed · Saudi energy ministry (Jazan); Allegation · Iran's Revolutionary Guards (mines)

events.title: Brent climbs to about $96, a third daily gain, in thin holiday trade
events.summary: Brent crude for January traded near $96 a barrel on Thursday 26 November, per Bloomberg; TASS reported it at $96.03 during the day, up 1.5%, with a high of $96.20. It was the third gain in a row; Bloomberg said Brent had risen almost 6% over the previous two sessions. Traders cited the strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, the Houthi claim on Ras Tanura and Iran's claim that two tankers hit mines near Hormuz. US markets were closed for Thanksgiving, so trading was thin, which can exaggerate price moves, and there was no settlement for US crude (WTI). Higher shipping through Hormuz this month and an expected supply surplus limited gains. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.
events.differs: One market report citing Reuters gives a settlement of $96.57, up $1.96; this could not be confirmed in a second source, so it is not used here.

events.title: Drone attack on a Kuwaiti air-defence site kills two Italian technicians; Kuwait blames Iran, which denies it
events.summary: Two Italian technicians working for the defence company Rheinmetall died after a drone attack on an air-defence surveillance site in Kuwait on 26 November, Italy's foreign ministry said. Italian authorities said they had been servicing the antennas of an anti-aircraft defence system. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were also hurt by falling debris. Kuwait's defence ministry called the attack "heinous Iranian aggression" against a "vital site", and Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the site was targeted by Iranian drones. An Iranian military spokesperson denied that Iran was responsible, per ABC News.
events.status: Confirmed · Italy's foreign ministry (deaths); Allegation · Kuwait, Italy (Iran's role)

events.title: US forces disable a ship trying to breach the blockade of Iran; Iran offers to help investigate the Kuwait attack
events.summary: The US military struck and disabled a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman after it left an Iranian port and tried to breach the US naval blockade despite repeated warnings, US Central Command said, per Gulf News and ABC's Good Morning America. The ship was not named. Iran's foreign ministry said Iran was ready to work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the origin" of Thursday's drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italian technicians, per Gulf News and The National. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran had "no role or involvement whatsoever". Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a tanker caught fire after hitting mines north of Oman's Al Ghanam Island; this has not been independently confirmed. Brent crude was up 0.95% at $97.49 a barrel on Friday morning UAE time and on track for a weekly gain of about 7%, per The National. OPEC+ meets on Sunday 29 November and is expected to keep its current policy, The National reported.
events.status: Stated · US Central Command; Stated · Iran's foreign ministry; Allegation · Iran's Revolutionary Guards (mine strike); Market data · The National
events.differs: Gulf News and CBS give different transcripts of what President Trump said about Iran at Mar-a-Lago on 26 November; both quote him as saying victory was at hand.
